The skip can control "social bonds" of people who know about it. It's not specified exactly what this means but it's clearly not good.

The containment is to surround it with a dozen people who have a random social structure, random knowledge of what's going on, and random goals (none of which actually matter). It's not said, but presumably the knowledge of this entity was erased from everyone else's mind. Each week the participants are reset and re-randomized, and some of them are swapped out with fresh personnel. This limits the changes the entity can make and probably also keeps it confused.

You (the reader) are starting a new shift. It may or may not be your first.

Per the required reading forum guidelines, please fill out the concept template to seek feedback on your idea:

Rather than posting a new comment, edit your previous post using the "edit" function under the "options" tab to the lower right of your first comment.

Remember that the combined text for your answers to the last four sections (Elevator Pitch, Central Narrative, Hook/Attention-Grabber, and Additional Notes) MAY NOT exceed 400 words. For convenience, authors can use this page to check wordcount: https://wordcounter.net/

As discussed on IRC this isn't very strong as a standalone piece, so I won't evaluate it as such, but I will want to evaluate its structure as a piece on progress.

An issue with this is that the fundamental stakes for the narrator/protagonist are not clear, except for that they have to wait a long time for a foregone conclusion. They clearly act during the time they are waiting, but their actions are actually glossed over and summarized. They don't appear to struggle to accomplish anything, even though they've accomplished a great amount of influence while they waited.

There was an opportunity here to create some amount of interesting nuance and contrast of simultaneously maintaining constant control and being completely out of control to act upon what has been gained, but I don't know if that was the intention of this piece. It was just something I noticed as a reader but the story didn't actually explore this.

item.title: Re: The Sandman (GREENLIGHT WANTED)
item.content:encoded:
I was summoned by IRC Chat. Let's crit this.

[+] Here, have some crit
[-] OK, now give me back my crit

Right of the bat, why don't you have the Seeking greenlight, Page Type, Genre, and Page Layout sections? Those don't add up to the word limit, and you should add them so reviewers know if you want greenlights, what type of page you want, what genre you're aiming for, etc.

Now, let's do the actual crit:

This humanoid makes any person they encounter a narcoleptic

Please specify if the humanoid chooses a person or it just affects anyone they encounter. I think it would be difficult for it to affect everyone. And if they chooses a person, does the person need to have any characteristics or it's just random?

they are lured into a sense of security before being murdered and/or eaten alive

Why? As I'm aware, the Ole Lukøje only punishes bad children. Why does this entity attacks people? Is it for food, fun, punishment…?

Central Narrative:

So my concern with your narrative is that it seems to have an escessive amount of references to the original story of the Ole Lukøje. While you can write something based off a fairy tale, you need to put some kind of twist to it, otherwise it would be just the same thing with the SCP logo slapped to it.

"The Ole Lukøje but now it's evil" isn't a good twist, at leat on my perspective. It seems cliché to just take a character and make it evil for no reason. Maybe you could write why did the Ole Lukøje become evil? Maybe an interview with the entity could clarify this? Maybe the researchers recognize him from old folktales and they are curious on why he is killing people now?

The other thing that concerns me is that all of your narrative is backstory. It's not wrong to focus on the backstory, but the only thing you're telling is how it came to Foundation custody. What happened after? I think an interview with the entity could improve your story.

Also, the “it killed me and it’ll kill you again" has no relation to what the SCP does after you wake up they were just spouting nonsense due to their new psychotic nature.

I think MTF members would be a lot more calm when waking up of a dream like this. Sure, they're afraid to die, but they're trained to face things like this. Maybe they would be worried and nervous, but they wouldn't be screaming like that.

Overall, I like stories based off pieces of literature, but I think this needs some kind of in-deep twist to differentiate it from the original story.

Feel free to contact a member of the Butterfly Squad to get more crit, or PM me to take another look.

Asked to take a look at this, apologies for the delay.

So like, the general shape of what you have here is good. It's a very emotional narrative, clear beginning and end, etc. But like, you're pulling a lot of elements into this, and it becomes a tad unfocused. Like, the Gate Guardian and 343 are extremely old and generally not looked upon fondly by modern audiences, as is your portrayal of the Serpent's Hand as a sort of… murderous, militarized force. You're also pulling stuff in from Three Moons — it's extremely all over the place in site lore, and I'd recommend you focus on one particular thing to make it work.

Question, err, how did O5-2 and Orpheus meet (and why do they have the names of greek characters)? Additionally, how did O5-2 let her guard slip enough to get killed? How did the information leak? Etc.

SCP 5127 was discovered in Chaco, Argentina in 2003 after civilians were consistently reporting deceased people rising from their graves.

SCP 5127 consists of SCP 5127-1 and SCP 5127-2. SCP 5127-1 is a strangely shaped book with covers made of an unknown harmful white substance and pages are made out of leather. The object appears to have the ability to resurrect deceased people.

Deleted at -23 and three votes.

Feedback Ported:

Iamwords2E

+ show block
– hide block

Format is confusing, you don't need to press enter every 2 lines that is just not how paragraphs work. Labeling of the instances is confusing, SCP-5127-2 and SCP-5127-3 could have their designations switched and it would flow better. Sentences are to simple and could be worded better so they are not as awkward. The SCP itself has little meat to and could use some plot (doesn't have to be a heavy one though) since at this point it is just the Necronomicon. You definitely have room for improvement but your asking for help is good sign. Though it is not recommended that you post articles on the main site of critique; The Wiki Sandbox in which drafts are posted for critique by designated wiki staff. Though I will warn you that it will likely be slow to hear a response though they are one of the better at giving critique that most other sources (even me). I hope this helps.

SCP-5136 is approximately 4 kilometers in length, 2 kilometers in width, and 100 meters in height, this anomaly is located in the Bahamas and is labeled “The Bahama Wonders Hotel”, the anomaly appears as a hotel, when the subject enters the Hotel they will be greeted by a man behind the desk, designated SCP-5136-1, he will be wearing formal attire. He will ask if the subject wishes to rent a room, if the subject says they are not they will be thrown out of the building from a strong force of wind, if the subject says they are looking for a room SCP-5136-2 will bring them to a random hallway, regardless if it is full or not, each hallway contains 40 doors leading to a room, these rooms are designated SCP-5136-2. For more information, read Addendum 1/332/CAI.

Deleted at -24 and three votes.

SCP-5156 is a mutated virus that came from an unknown planet. It's appearance is a genderless Humanoid-shaped figure that has arms twirling uncontrollably every second for an odd reason. SCP-5156's capabilities are yet to be understood, but the one discovered is regeneration. SCP-5156's regeneration from wounds and such is absurd, it has come to a point where SCP-5156 can regenerate a limb for approximately 3 seconds. Sightings of SCP-5156 have been spotted in ██████. Thankfully, only a handful of people saw it. Further research of SCP-5156 is ordered by the 05 Council. Reports and Investigation will be available to those of Level 4+ Clearance.

Deleted at -20 and three votes.

The supplementary pages SCP-5156 Investigation 001 and SCP-5156 Research Log 001 have likewise been deleted at -19 and -23 respectivley.

SCP-5234 resembles the nozzle of a common garden hose at its shortest length, but can expand and will most often be seen around 10 centimeters long. The "hose" will grow indefinitely, but its rate of growth differs depending on the environment. When any part of the "hose" is near plant life, SCP-5234 will rapidly elongate, and the longest recorded length has been one kilometer . SCP-5234 has been recorded to grow quicker around materials made of formerly organic material, such as wood, but it grows at its fastest rate when near live plants. SCP-5234 grows at its slowest when contained in a container of volcanic rock, with the most efficient type being obsidian.

Deleted at -15 and three votes.

Feedback Ported:

Raitia

+ show block
– hide block

It's a creative concept for a non-agressive euclid, playing with the idea of a hose snake, that literally plays a game of snake with the enviroment, but it feels… underwhelming? The rust tidbit with rusting blood feels mostly like a danger for danger's sake addition, and beyond that it doesn't really do much more than slither around and grow. The containment procedures are also unnecessarily long and don't make sense. If It grows in organic material and destroys metal, why not just stick it in something like plastic?

SCP-5187 is a paperback book of the title The Whole Art of Deduction, however instances of SCP-5187 have been located with minor alterations to the title. Additionally, the author is credited variously under names associated with the fictional detective Sherlock Holmes. Efforts to trace the origins of these books have succeeded only in uncovering now-defunct publishing companies and publication dates for each book consistent with the final year of operation of each company.

When observed SCP-5961 appears to be being of, what has been described as, ‘indescribable beauty’ by human beings observing it. This beauty is believed to overload dopamine production in the observer’s brain, creating an addiction to seeing and pleasing SCP-5961.

item.title: {Seeking Greenlight} The Devil You Know
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes
Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Weird

Elevator Pitch: This creature resembles a demonic humanoid borne from human consciousness with a key anomaly embedded in its infectious presence. Anyone that either directly observes it or indirectly through secondhand description becomes convinced them to be a long-forgotten friend or lover they remember fondly, regardless whether said witnesses has any actual history with subject.
Subject also possesses the ability to instantly teleport close by to anyone familiar with the entity’s existence, manifesting instantaneously around corners or behind doors. Whenever someone becomes informed about this creature, that person is immediately “marked” as a potential anchor destination for teleportation.
Individuals who become more familiar with the subject heavily favors its opinion over even their closest peers, occupying their minds to near obsession. Individuals experiencing excess time spent in its presence become entirely occupied by thoughts of the entity, abandoning loved ones, and even disregarding basic needs like food or shelter in more extreme cases.
The most notable and bizarre feature to this process, however, is that continued exposure to the demon’s anomalous presence is capable of erasing of any pre-existing mental manipulative affects placed upon any human’s psyche. Intervals of necessary exposure to the demon’s presence to perform this varies from days to years, depending on how powerful said previous manipulative alterations were. This property may indeed prove valuable to the foundation, though anyone proven to acknowledge devil's existence from both direct or indirect sources can only be remedied with large doses of Class A amnestic.

Central Narrative: The demon was borne out of an unknown man’s own sacrifice to ritualistically create something from the collective unconscious of humanity. Subject finds mild entertainment in playing with the strings of the human mind it has such a great intuitive understanding about, preferring to use his powers to minimize aggression in his presence. It holds little empathy for humanity, though its indifference allows rare opportunities for it to cooperate with something that might grapple its attention; typically whatever may, in the subject’s words, “make these mundane hours more interesting.”

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The devil can be dangerous due to its powerful and evocative aura and teleportative capabilities, but it can also be utilized to counteract active influence mind-affecting SCP creatures.

Tags: compulsion, empathetic, humanoid, infohazard, mind-affecting, keter, sapient, sentient, teleportation

item.title: Re: Twister (green light seeking)
item.content:encoded:
I'm not qualified to give greenlights, but I'm having a hard time seeing an authorized greenlighter doing so. You've clearly made an attempt to address the narrative needs of the article, but,

The thing inside seems to be emitting lots of free energy, people are trying to get to it and use it.

is not an interesting narrative. At best it's one story beat. A successful story usually uses multiple beats to build tension, intrigue the reader, build characters and/or worlds, or all of the above. What you've described does none of these things. It's just an event that happens.

On top of this the anomaly is described in a stunted, confusing way and just isn't interesting on its own OR with the story. In the future, maybe you could try coming up with a story first, and then designing the details of the anomaly around what would make the most interesting narrative.

Regardless, I hope you have a good day.

item.title: First SCP.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: A well liked butcher in the area turns out to be empowered by the power of the flesh to produce the best cuts.

Central Narrative: A story of a Polish sarkite who flees his community during the chaos at the end of WWI and emigrates to America for a normal life. He finds work running a butcher shop and deli. He's able to do this by cloning beef and pork and manipulating it to be the best possible cut of meat to work with. This causes him to be popular and wealthy as he doesn't need to keep buying new meat. It does cause people to spread rumors about mob ties as he sometimes talks to scary looking men who aren't from the area. He dies and tells his son to not get involved in sarkicism, that the UIU and Foundation will deal with any problems about it, and that he' a good enough butcher to not need flesh warping powers.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Turns out the butcher who everyone thinks has mob ties and might be a cannibal is actually neither. Though the truth isn't all that comforting

Additional Notes: This is my second idea for my first SCP. The basic feed back from my first try a few weeks ago basically boiled down to it being too similar to another SCP and not very narrative. So I put that idea on the back burner and came up with something I thought would be more narrative.

Leaving aside the fact that this is supposed to be a report on SCP-5927 and its containment, repeating its scp number on the description could get a little repetive, as its basically its name, repeating your "main character's" name over and over on a story is not ussually a good thing, maybe change some of them to "the entity" or "it" would be great.

as kind of unnecesary information, by this point in the report the reader knows very well what the skip does with its friky light tentacles, might as well feed on them or instantly break their spines, the agents are killed by the entity, i dont think knowing it eat something while killing them tells me anything important

And this last is probably the most subjective but i find it weird that the victim of this SCP is refferd as a PoI and not SCP-5927-1 as most other skips do, i mean, wondertainment is a PoI, a soon-to-be skip brunch is not a person of interest, at least as the foundation is concerned.

All that aside is a spooky monster being contained in an interesting way so i say this is a good one, i havent yet rated an article but i say you get my first +1 good sir/lady. Have a nice day.

item.title: Snatcher Slug (Seeking Critique)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Not yet

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is an SCP that can attach itself to a host, designated SCP-XXXX-1, in the form of a small slug that slowly feeds off of its host until the host is completely alone from anyone else and is isolated somewhere where it can not be detected killing them. It then pumps a potent, instantly acting neurotoxin into their bloodstream and assimilates as them, eating them for nutrition. SCP-XXXX then goes around as SCP-XXXX-1, designated as -2 from that point. It releases more small instances of SCP-XXXX that repeat the process, and after a period of two years, -2 dies. SCP-XXXX can infect any sufficiently complex organism, and inherits all abilities of that organism. It has been observed assimilating with dogs, cats, and even a juvenile Kokomo dragon. A definite way to detect -2 is to take a Copper or Gold wire heated to at least 15° Celsius and submerge it lightly in a blood sample of -2. When the wire touches the blood, it jumps away. Containing it is somewhat difficult, as it can assimilate into anyone and can not be killed with regular firearms. Instead, to permanently destroy or severely incapacitate it requires using incendiary weaponry. It can survive in pretty much any environment, but to contain it, there is a small room, where over the course of a day, 12 gallons of pig's blood is pumped in for XXXX. The room has 14 different cameras with overlapping sight lines. Past that room is an airlock where there are flamethrower countermeasures installed and infrared scanners to detect the abnormally high body temperature of XXXX.

Central Narrative: A Foundation Research team of twelve researchers are moving to investigate an odd increase in the electromagnetic pulses emanating from the South Pole. They find a large asteroid buried under some ice that seems to have been there for at least 120.000 years, unearthed by melting ice. The team takes back a large canister filled with slugs back to Site-118 for study, but the organisms assimilate with them and manage to destroy the base. MTF Upsilon-6 "Cold Shoulder" (I couldn't find an MTF Squadron with the description I needed so I made one up) attempts to retrieve the scientists, unknowingly bringing back instances of -2 to Site-29, which spreads the infection of XXXX. It is recaptured and contained at Site-29, where the slugs are contained.

The article then follows the efforts of the Foundation to track down and contain the clones of the people they killed (most of whom have reintegrated into society), robbing them of their second chance. Evidence begins to show that a guilty rogue researcher may have planted the SCP deliberately to resurrect a D-class they were attached to.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A heart-wrenching story of love, loss, reanimation, and what happens when a second chance at life isn't enough.

item.title: Re: SCP Idea (Seeking Greenlight): Elaine of Astolat's Curse
item.content:encoded:
Answers:

  • I don't think I said they 'feed' on vanity. SCP-XXXX-1 may use their castors vanity in their judgements/insults but not always. SCP-XXXX-1 will use anything to insults their castors. Also, all of this stems from the one important element. Reflections aren't naturally meant to reflect their castors. SCP-XXXX is the reason reflections act like reflections. Her maintaining her gaze in a way 'imprisons' reflections, forcing them to copy their castors actions every minute of every day. Think about how maddening that is. When SCP-XXXX-1 occurs, the reflections are going to use every possible second of freedom to emphasise how sickening it is being trapped. They don't just want to insult them. They want to degrade them. To put it simply, reflections are enslaved by their castors and the castors only discover this when SCP-XXXX-1 occurs. Then think about how the castors feel when they learn this. They've basically learnt that every reflection they cast is someone looking back at them, judging and hating them.
  • Also If you recall, I mentioned SCP-XXXX has a reflective coating on her inner eyelids. Whoever had her before the Foundation managed to coat her eyelids with this material. This is how she is able to blink and sleep. Now, one of the clinchers I have planned is to do with the decaying process. Her eyelid coatings are also decaying. Slowly but still at a noticeable rate. And unfortunately, the Foundation doesn't know how to replicate the material used to make it. Meaning, a day will come when her eyelid coating doesn't work anymore. Now the Foundations has a real problem!
  • Her mutilations are tied to why she doesn't age. Remember, she doesn't cause SCP-XXXX-1 but stops it from happening. Meaning, if she dies, SCP-XXXX-1 is permanent. So to prevent this from happening, her previous captors did something to make her immortal. They also gave her her eyelid coating. This is why she is scarred and mutilated. Her captors weren't doing out of malevolence or coldness. They did it to ensure SCP-XXXX-1 wouldn't be permanent. All of this would be explained in the interview with her. I didn't talk about it because I was already at 394 words.
  • SCP-XXXX-1 is an event in which peoples reflections return to their natural independent state. This event has a time frame and after a while, the reflections return to reflecting their castors. That's what I meant by resynchronised.

That sentence in particular isn't exactly reflective of the Foundationverse's geopolitics. The Foundation is certainly trusted by nations to do its job, but America, Russia, and the UN set up their own organizations since theirs and the Foundation's ideologies aren't the exact same.

In reality, there's a bunch of rivalry and hostility between the Foundation and PENTAGRAM, the GOC, and GRU Division "P" (when they were active). The Foundation can be interpreted as a kind of neutral party here, which America finds to be useful but not totally helpful in furthering their national interests. Similar story for the UN, since their beliefs often place them in opposition to the Foundation, and same with Russia during the Cold War.

In essence, other national groups exist because the nations that sponsor them have specific goals that the Foundation couldn't fulfill, whether that be supremacy on the world stage or the destruction of the anomalous.

item.title: Re: They Just Keep Searching
item.content:encoded:
Thanks so much for the feedback, I really appreciate it regardless of your experience - it's always good to have a fresh pair of eyes on things.

Please let me know if you remember what you think this sounds similar to. I had a search around the wiki before I started seriously considering the idea but the closest things I could find were:
SCP-988 - a wooden box that cannot be opened as all attempts are "conveniently" interrupted, but this is its only anomalous trait.
SCP-216 - the only real similarity with this one is the fact that it's a kind of safe.
SCP-902 - a box that emits a ticking noise people become convinced is counting down. It does compel people to open the box, but it CAN be opened and doesn't appear to contain anything, so I figured it was different enough from this one to be its own thing.

As for the rest, some of those questions I do have answers for but didn't have space to detail them in the initial post due to the word limit. I have written an SCP draft for this idea to help organise my thoughts about it - I won't link it here as it hasn't been specifically asked for but I'll use info from it to answer your questions.

+ show block
– hide block

1: I go into quite a lot of detail about this in the draft. There are exact measurements given for width, length, ceiling height and floor thickness of the SCP's cell to ensure no accidental exposure. A circular hazard warning line is also painted on the floor around the hazardous zone so people can avoid it if they have to go in the cell.

2: The anomalous effect isn't triggered by staring at the safe, it's triggered by spacial proximity. Anyone within 10 m of the safe is affected - you could be affected without even knowing the safe is there initially, and it seems completely unremarkable until roughly the 3 hour mark. Those 3 hours are cumulative so if you were to spend 10 minutes in the hazardous zone each day, you would become infected after roughly 18 days. The discovery report explains that it was found in the basement of a house, with the proximity zone edging out into other parts of the house so the inhabitants were affected over time. Though I may have to increase the zone to 15 or 20 m to make this more believable, so thanks for highlighting that. I did consider making the amount of time much shorter, but then I couldn't think of a conceivable way for Foundation staff to transport the safe without being infected.

3: We don't know - I wanted that to be part of the mystery. The safe appears centuries old (though impossible to properly analyse), but Foundation researchers reportedly argue that if it were as old as it looks it would have been found earlier due to its effects. So it could be an ancient artifact of unknown origin, or something an anomalous entity recently made for a laugh and just made it LOOK old. As I mentioned, it is found in a basement after police investigate due to violence committed by an SCP-XXXX-1 instance who resided there.

4: As above, we don't know for sure. Though it feels unlikely to me that any non-anomalous humans could create it.

5: No, the surface is impenetrable by measuring equipment as well as weapons - all attempts at observing the contents have yielded no results.

6: 280 kg.

7: After the 3 hours of exposure they can transform fully at any time between a few hours and 2 days after the fact. Exact length varies depending on the individual, but none have been less than 2 hours and none have been more than 2 full days.

8: Yes. As previously mentioned, observing the safe is not the hazardous part. As long as you're more than 10 m away you're fine. However, the SCP can affect cameras as all cameras monitoring it spontaneously deactivate during its active episodes.

9: Nobody has yet been harmed by the safe itself. Though the incident report of cameras being deactivated and motion sensors being tripped MAY imply there's an entity inside the safe that can leave and may be harmful, but no harm has been done yet and the safe itself could just be affecting electronics without anything leaving it - I wanted that to be open to interpretation.

Thanks for the questions, and the naming suggestions too! I like "Isolated Safe" quite a lot but I wonder if it's too similar to SCP-216's "The Safe". I will definitely consider all of those suggestions though! :)
